significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a "low-dimensional, causally manipulable subspace" controls reasoning length and that moving along it can shorten traces while retaining accuracy over a moderate range; this is principally a form-(ii) causal claim of the separable-direction-plus-steering-repair template, with a weak threshold prediction in the proposed accuracy-length "cliff." It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon—smooth length control with an accuracy-preserving region—and a mechanism for that single behavior, but it does not determine how to select the right compute budget per problem, a central issue in adaptive test-time-compute work such as Snell et al. (2024), while activation steering work such as Turner et al. (2023) and Rimsky et al. (2024) shows the practical meaning of this intervention class. Verified false, it would usefully rule out a compact linear control account or a broad "free-lunch" shortening regime, although it would not discriminate among nonlinear, distributed, or problem-dependent alternatives; true and false therefore denote distinguishable states. Topic-substitution check: efficient reasoning alone would not earn this score—the specific causal length axis and accuracy plateau add a definite conclusion—but the conclusion remains bounded to one efficiency behavior, placing it only slightly above the topic's obvious first hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handle is a "training-free, interpretable dial for compute allocation," instantiated by the proposed length-steering vector and its coefficient. It is ex ante because it is applied at inference before the remaining reasoning trace is generated, leaving an action window for practitioners controlling serving cost rather than merely explaining an observed failure. However, after recalibration on another model the conclusion predicts only that researchers should look for a suitable low-dimensional direction, not its location, coefficient-length curve, or accuracy threshold; moreover, "test whether a single vector generalizes across tasks and layers" leaves cross-task transfer unresolved and asserts no cross-architecture or cross-training-regime law. Topic-substitution check: the topic alone supplies no such inference-time knob, so the claim has genuine additional reach, but its model-dependent vector and uncertain scope keep it near the topic median rather than in the broadly transferable-relation band.
